tips: Load your Suica/Pasmo into Apple/Google Wallet before landing at MSP so you can tap straight through the train gates.
Hit the ATM at Haneda or a 7-Eleven konbini upon arrival; with the USD/JPY rate at ~162, withdrawing JPY in-country yields the best exchange rates.

2026-12-16.weatherAlert: Typical December in Tokyo is cold and dry, but occasional rain is possible. The afternoon and evening are heavily outdoor-focused (Shibuya Sky, Blue Cave illumination).

suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Miyashita Park covered rooftop + Parco + Tower Records
suggestedSwap.reason: If it rains, the outdoor Blue Cave walk loses its magic and gets miserable; the covered Miyashita Park and Parco complex keeps the squad dry and entertained.

tips: Shibuya Sky often sells out; if you didn't book in advance, use the Mag's Park rooftop or Shibuya Hikarie 11F Sky Lobby for a free alternative crossing view.
December evenings are chilly—grab a heat-tech layer from Uniqlo before standing outside for the Blue Cave.

2026-12-17.weatherAlert: Risk of cold rain for the outdoor Nakamise snack gauntlet and Ueno Ameyoko market.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Ueno Ameyoko market under the tracks
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Tokyo National Museum (samurai swords + armor, 2h)
suggestedSwap.reason: If it rains, the open-air Ameyoko market is less enjoyable; the Tokyo National Museum is right next door, indoors, and world-class.

tips: Senso-ji is best before 9:00 AM to avoid the densest crowds at Nakamise-dori.
Skytree can have insane evening queues; the Asahi Beer Hall's 22F Sky Room next door offers the same river view for the price of a beer.
teamLab Planets requires stepping into water—wear easy slip-off shoes and roll up your pants.
Golden Gai bars are tiny (many cap at 4-6 people); split into smaller groups of 2-3 to actually get seats.

2026-12-19.weatherAlert: High risk of cold, wet, and windy conditions for the coastal Enoshima tram and island climb. December winds can make the Sea Candle viewing deck brutally cold.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Enoshima island — climb to the Sea Candle
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Enoshima onsen finish: Enospa overlooks the bay
suggestedSwap.reason: If the weather turns foul, climbing an exposed island in the wind is miserable; Enospa offers a warm soak with the same bay/Fuji view.

tips: The Enoden coastal tram is beautiful but slow; if connecting from Hase-dera, check the timetable so you don't wait 30 minutes on a cold platform.
If the sky is overcast, the 'Fuji over Sagami Bay' sunset will be a bust—skip the Enoshima sunset wait and head back early for a cozy Shinjuku dinner.
Ghibli Museum tickets sell out instantly; if you didn't secure them, the 'consolation bracket' of Inokashira Park and Shimokitazawa is a fantastic, low-stress morning.
Run the Airbnb laundry during dinner so everyone packs a clean kit for the Kyoto move tomorrow.

2026-12-21.weatherAlert: Gion at golden hour and the Kamo River bank are exposed to December winds; rain will make the Shirakawa canal walk less picturesque.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Kamo River bank — konbini cans, December stars
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Kyoto International Manga Museum
suggestedSwap.reason: If it's raining, sitting on the cold Kamo riverbank is a miserable end to the night; the Manga Museum is an incredible, massive indoor time vortex to stay warm and dry.

tips: Grab an ekiben (train bento) at Tokyo Station before boarding the Nozomi—minute 40 on the left side gives the Fuji view.
Pontocho Alley is narrow and gets crowded; even with a reservation for 8, be prepared to wait a few minutes for table assembly.

2026-12-22.weatherAlert: Fushimi Inari at dawn in December is freezing. Rain makes the mountain trails extremely slippery.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: FUSHIMI INARI AT DAWN — the whole reason alarms exist
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Sanjusangendo — 1,001 golden Kannon statues
suggestedSwap.reason: If it's raining heavily, the steep stone paths of Fushimi Inari become slippery and the cold is biting; Sanjusangendo is indoors, jaw-dropping, and criminally underrated.

tips: Layer up aggressively for Fushimi Inari—you will warm up hiking, but standing still at the top in the wind is freezing.
Funaoka Onsen is a historic, tattoo-friendly sento; the 'electric bath' is an experience, but don't stay in too long!

2026-12-23.weatherAlert: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove before the buses is highly exposed to cold December rain, which washes out the magical forest lighting.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove before the buses exist
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: SNOW PROTOCOL (overrides everything): Kyoto wakes up white → Kinkaku-ji at opening
suggestedSwap.reason: If it snows (or heavy rain), the bamboo grove is dreary and crowded with umbrellas; Kinkaku-ji in the snow is Japan's rarest and most breathtaking photo op.

tips: Wakakusa-yama is closed for the winter (closes Dec 13)—do not attempt the climb.
When feeding the Nara deer, bow first and show empty hands when done; never run, as they will chase you.

2026-12-24.crowdAlert: KFC on Christmas Eve is wildly popular in Japan; if you want the sacred bucket, you must pre-order online weeks in advance or expect massive lines.
tips: If you missed the Nintendo Museum lottery, Uji's Byodo-in and Tsuen tea make for a fantastic, low-stress morning anyway.
Split your takoyaki crawl: get a half-plate from 2-3 different stands (Wanaka, Kukuru, Juhachiban) rather than filling up at the first stop.

2026-12-25.crowdAlert: USJ on Christmas Day will be at peak capacity; Super Nintendo World timed entry is a brutal sprint if you don't have Express Passes.
tips: Rope-drop the park 45 minutes early and sprint directly to Super Nintendo World to secure your timed entry or app reservation.
If Kinopio's Café has a 2-hour wait, grab a Yoshi snack stand item and focus on the Power-Up Band challenges instead.

2026-12-26.weatherAlert: Miyajima island and the floating torii are highly exposed to cold sea winds and rain; the ferry ride can be choppy and miserable in bad weather.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: ITSUKUSHIMA SHRINE — the torii floating in the sea
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Energy honesty: skip Miyajima, do the museum unhurried, meet at Hiroshima station
suggestedSwap.reason: If the weather is terrible, the ferry and exposed island walk are freezing and the torii view is obscured; spending more reflective time at the Peace Museum is a worthy alternative.

tips: This is the longest day of the trip; if anyone is redlining, it's completely fine to skip Miyajima and rest at a cafe near Hiroshima station.
Check the Miyajima tide times in advance—the torii 'floating' effect only happens at high tide; at low tide, you can walk out to it in the mud.
551 Horai butaman (pork buns) sell out nightly; grab a 4-pack from Namba station BEFORE your crab dinner to secure breakfast for the house.
Midosuji Illumination is best walked south as the lights guide you toward Namba; start at Umeda Sky Building and walk down.
Himeji Castle involves a lot of steep, cold stair climbs in December—dress in warm, flexible layers.
Do your final tax-free shopping tonight; ensure receipts are stapled in your passports and purchases are accessible for customs on Dec 29.
For the shinkansen ride east, book seats on the LEFT side (Row A/E) for Mount Fuji's encore around minute 90.
Zero out your Suica card by buying last-minute snacks/gatchapon at Haneda; most transit cards cannot be refunded for cash easily.

globalTips: With the USD/JPY rate at ~162, your dollar goes far—withdraw JPY at 7-Eleven or Japan Post ATMs for the best exchange rates, and avoid airport currency exchanges which have poor rates and high fees.
December in Japan is cold and dry, but occasional rain is possible; pack versatile, non-cotton layers (heat-tech, windbreakers) and a compact travel umbrella for sudden showers.

For a group of 8, always split into smaller squads of 2-4 for restaurants, bars (especially Golden Gai), and crowded trains—Japan's venues are rarely built for large groups, and splitting up is the fastest way to get seated.
